title: v1: launch and status with TOML config, matching the current shell launcher
description:
## Why

Replace a personal shell launcher that grew Python snippets and broke twice. The launcher already makes the decision rota exists for; it needs to become a tested Rust tool with its personal details moved into a config file.

## Scope

- Backends:
  - agy (Antigravity CLI);
  - an sclaude-style second Claude account: `claude` run with its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`;
  - Codex (`codex` with its own `CODEX_HOME`);
  - OpenCode;
  - the main Claude config as a last fallback.
- Quota readers per backend, borrowing the approaches in docs/references.md (caam, T3 Code's usage readers, OpenCode's Go usage schema, Codex's RateLimitSnapshot).
- One-at-a-time caps per backend through a process scan or a lock.
- Round-robin across available backends.
- Role and level to model (and effort) mapping in TOML.
- The guard check: refuse a backend whose configured command guard (for example dcg) is not installed.
- An atomic trusted-folder edit where a CLI needs it (agy stops at a trust prompt for an untrusted folder).
- `rota status --json`.
- `rota launch --dry-run`.

## Behavior reference

The reference is the personal shell launcher `agent-launch.sh` (kept outside this repository). Its behavior, without its personal paths or numbers:

- Usage: `[--role implement|review] [--level medium|high] [--only BACKEND] [--dry-run] <prompt file>`, run from the agent's working directory. Bad options or a missing prompt file exit 2.
- Level picks the model or effort: high maps to the top model or effort on each backend, medium to the next one down.
- Role picks the allowed backends: implementers may use agy, the second Claude account and Codex; reviewers only agy and the second Claude account. `--only` narrows the set and must be allowed for the role.
- Each backend check yields available or not, plus a reading line:
  - agy: requires the dcg guard hook in agy's hooks config, then reads `agy -p /usage` (tab-separated lines: group, limit name, "<n>%", reset time) and needs the five-hour and weekly remaining percentages of the "Claude and GPT models" group at or above per-role minimums.
  - Second Claude account: requires stored credentials; probes the usage endpoint with the stored access token; if the probe fails, wakes the account with one tiny prompt and probes again (never in a dry run, which must not spend a turn). Needs five-hour and seven-day used percentages under per-role limits; a missing window counts as under.
  - Codex: refuses in folders configured as belonging to another (work) account, runs an account check, then needs every quota window above 0% remaining.
- Caps: the second Claude account and agy each allow one running session at a time. A running session is found by scanning processes (the claude executable with that `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, including through a symlinked path; any agy process except a /usage probe).
- Round-robin: keeps the last pick in a state file and takes the first available backend after it, in a fixed order.
- No backend available: reviews and `--only` refuse (exit 3) with all readings; implementers fall back to the main Claude config, logged loudly.
- Every decision is logged with time, folder, role, level and all readings.
- `--dry-run` prints the pick and the command (the prompt shown as `$(cat file)`) and changes nothing, including the state file.
- Before launching agy, adds the folder to agy's `trustedWorkspaces` setting with an atomic write that keeps other keys and the file mode.
- Codex runs interactive and unattended, with approvals and sandbox off; the guard hook still checks every command.
- The launch replaces the launcher process (exec).

## Out of scope

- Mid-session failover.
- Account switching within one provider.
- Eon integration.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests for each quota parser, with fixtures of made-up data.
- Unit tests for the rotation and the caps.
- Unit tests for config validation.
- A dry run that matches the shell script's decision on the same readings.
- An example config in the repository with placeholder values only; personal paths, accounts and thresholds live in the user's config file.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test`
- One real launch of each backend in a scratch folder.
